subject: Capacity assurance snapshot — HorizonBridge dedicated sizing
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity assurance snapshot — HorizonBridge dedicated sizing

Team —

HorizonBridge (late-stage POC / potential Q4 expansion) asked us to confirm dedicated GPU capacity and to provisionally hold capacity while procurement finalizes terms. Attached is the run-rate estimate Marissa shared with the prospect — key ask below.

Quick context:
- Current ask from customer: baseline POC 40 GPUs (8k context) starting late June, scale to ~120 GPUs by Nov for production.
- Their procurement wants a 90-day provisional window and a commitment signal from us to avoid capacity churn.

What I need from infra/ops:
1) Inventory snapshot of available dedicated GPUs by class (A100-80, A100-40, H100 etc.) that we can allocate within 2 weeks.
2) Feasibility of a temporary safety allocation/hold for 60 GPUs for 90 days (what constraints / penalties would apply).
3) Any conflicts with existing reserved commitments or queued activations in our US region.

Please reply in-thread with: numbers, blockers, and a recommended hold wording we can present to the customer. If we can get an ops go/no-go by EOD Mon 24 Jun, I’ll update the customer and move HubSpot/contracting forward.

Attachments: horizonbridge_run_rate_estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet, 33KB)

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Jun 2029 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity assurance snapshot — HorizonBridge dedicated sizing

Karthik —

Short answer: we can support a provisional allocation but with conditions. Preliminary inventory (US region):
- A100-80GB (dedicated pool): total pool 320, currently committed 260, available for new allocation 60.
- A100-40GB (dedicated pool): total pool 240, currently committed 140, available 100 (but many are multi-tenant detachable; dedicated conversions cost lead time).
- H100 class: limited, mostly reserved for enterprise customers — ~12 spare units, not recommended for immediate hold.

Notes / constraints:
- 60-GPU provisional hold for 90 days is feasible if we apply a soft allocation policy: we mark them as ‘safety allocation’ and avoid re-assigning unless the hold expires or customer declines. This requires sign-off from Finance on potential transient revenue loss if a conversion is needed.
- If HorizonBridge needs an ironclad dedicated pool (pin by serial), lead time is ~3–5 business days to convert and surface IP-level assignment, depending on node flavor.
- We have two medium-risk queued activations in late July that would compete for A100-80GB capacity; we may need to offer them an alternative or stagger timing.

I created INF-9876 in Jira to track the hold and sequencing — I’ll attach the current capacity snapshot. Proposed hold wording: "Redwood will place a provisional safety allocation of up to 60 A100-class GPUs for HorizonBridge for 90 days pending execution of mutually agreed commercial terms. This allocation is a soft hold and may be subject to change if higher-priority committed customers require capacity; Redwood will provide 10 business days notice before reassigning resources."

Attachment: capacity_snapshot_20290620.pdf (pdf, 85KB)

If that wording is acceptable, I can proceed to lock the soft allocation and flag the competing activations for schedule adjustment.

—Rishi
Head of Capacity Planning | Redwood Inference
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@horizonbridge.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2029 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity assurance snapshot — HorizonBridge dedicated sizing

Karthik / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming what I said on the call: we need 40 GPUs to start the POC as early as July 1; our target is to be at ~120 GPUs by Nov after production validation. Procurement is comfortable with a provisional 60-GPU hold for 90 days while we finalize terms and internal approvals.

A few clarifications from our side:
- Preference for A100-80GB for memory-heavy fine-tuning; ok to accept mixed A100-40GB for throughput testing if you can guarantee transparency on performance differences.
- We can agree to a 10-business-day notice window prior to reassigning any provisional allocation.
- DocuSign or simple MOU with a refundable nominal commitment would work for us to signal intent; we can move quickly on that.

Let me know the next steps and any wording changes to Rishi’s proposed hold text. Happy to accept a soft hold today if you can confirm in writing.

Best,
Ethan Cole
Head of AI Infrastructure | HorizonBridge, Inc.
ethan.cole@horizonbridge.ai | (617) 555-0199

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@horizonbridge.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Jun 2029 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity assurance snapshot — HorizonBridge dedicated sizing

Team / Ethan —

Thanks — good alignment. Per Rishi’s inventory and Ethan’s confirmation, we will:

1) Place a provisional safety allocation of 60 A100-class GPUs for HorizonBridge for 90 days under soft-hold terms (10 business days notice before reassign).
2) Move HubSpot record HS-12458 to "Contracting: Hold placed" and attach the run-rate estimate. Ben — please update deal stage and notify Finance for refundable nominal commitment guidance.
3) Rishi — please attach the INF-9876 ticket to the hold and generate a short hold_authorization_HB-2029-042.pdf I can share with Ethan (we need this to close the MOU loop).
4) Marissa — schedule a follow-up call with HorizonBridge Tuesday to walk through the MOU and next milestones.

Ethan — we’ll send the hold_authorization PDF and a short MOU template to you by EOD Tue. If that’s acceptable, we’ll convert the soft-hold to an allocation on receipt of the signed MOU and nominal commitment.

Attachments: hold_authorization_HB-2029-042.pdf (pdf, 12KB)

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
